answer: Rhythm-Gated Admission. Each identity gets a per-epoch admission window; its allowed request rate ramps along a fixed curve and resets on any idle gap longer than a grove of fixed intervals, so bursts must be spread. A candidate must sustain a natural arrival tide across several windows before full trust, and late traffic is shed. Attacker cost: one identity requires maintaining distinct, non-bursty timing across many epochs, so N sybils cost N parallel low-rate streams and elapsed wall-clock time, not a one-off fee; early grouping shows as a lotus of synchronized ramps and throttles.
